analysis: The code snippet defines a private method parseInt0 that parses an integer from a CharSequence. It calls charAt twice: first at the start with index p, and later inside a loop with incrementing p. The charAt method throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if the index is negative or not less than the sequence length. The code does not validate that p is non-negative or that p and lim are within the bounds of the sequence. The only check is 'if (lim == p)' which does not ensure valid indices. Consequently, if p is negative or >= sequence.length(), the first charAt will throw IndexOutOfBoundsException. Similarly, if lim > sequence.length(), the loop will eventually call charAt with an index equal to sequence.length() (or larger) causing the exception. Thus the throwing condition is not avoided.
answer: The only exception declared by charAt is IndexOutOfBoundsException. Its throwing conditions (index negative or >= length) are not avoided in the code.
remark: IndexOutOfBoundsException can be triggered in two scenarios: (1) if the initial index p is negative or greater than or equal to the length of the sequence, the first call sequence.charAt(p) will fail; (2) if the parameter lim is greater than the sequence length, the loop condition p < lim will cause charAt(p) to be called with an index that eventually becomes equal to or exceeds the sequence length, resulting in the exception.
